title: DART-FL: Burst-Aware Multitask Federated Learning under Dynamic Inference Demand at the Edge
abstract: arXiv:2608.27713v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Edge intelligence systems increasingly require model training and online inference to coexist on resource-constrained devices, while inference demand can vary substantially across tasks over time. This creates two coupled challenges: sufficient computation must be reserved for inference to maintain service-level objectives (SLOs), while the remaining training capacity should adapt to task-specific demand so that frequently requested tasks can improve earlier during training.   We propose an SLO-aware, demand-driven multitask federated learning framework (DART-FL) that jointly adapts the inference-training resource split and task-level training emphasis. At each scheduling interval, DART-FL uses the inference backlog and profiled service capacity to determine the minimum resource allocation required for inference. tldr: 该论文提出DART-FL框架，一种SLO感知、需求驱动的多任务联邦学习方法，能够在边缘设备上联合优化推理与训练的资源分配，并根据任务需求动态调整各任务的训练优先级，以应对动态变化且存在突发的推理需求。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes DART-FL, an SLO-aware, demand-driven multitask federated learning framework that jointly adapts the inference-training resource split and task-level training emphasis on edge devices to handle dynamic and bursty inference demand.
